0.long_answer: The specialized cilia referred to in the question are known as nodal cilia. These are a type of motile cilia present on the cells of the embryonic node, and they play a critical role in establishing left-right asymmetry during human development. Unlike typical motile cilia, nodal cilia lack the central pair of microtubules and instead exhibit a rotational movement that generates a leftward fluid flow. This fluid flow is essential in triggering the asymmetric placement of the internal organs. In primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), mutations and resulting dysfunction in these nodal cilia can lead to improper or random determination of left-right position, which may result in conditions such as situs inversus, where organs are mirrored from their normal positions.
